items.title: Tulmimetostat Plus Luxdegalutamide in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing the combination of two investigational drugs, tulmimetostat (DZR123) and luxdegalutamide (JSB462), versus standard care in patients with progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). This trial is currently recruiting patients. The study aims to evaluate both the safety and effectiveness of this novel drug combination.

items.title: Opevesostat Phase 3 Trial for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing opevesostat (MK-5684) plus hormone therapy against switching to another hormonal agent (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in mCRPC patients who previously received one hormonal therapy. The study is recruiting and aims to determine if opevesostat can prevent cancer progression longer than switching hormonal agents. This is an important trial testing a new drug mechanism.

items.title: Zanzalintinib After Pluvicto in Chemotherapy-Naive Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial evaluating zanzalintinib in mCRPC patients after receiving Pluvicto (lutetium-177 PSMA therapy) who have not yet received chemotherapy. The trial will assess whether this targeted drug can continue controlling cancer after radioligand therapy. Study has not yet started recruiting patients.

items.title: Creatine and Resistance Training to Preserve Muscle Mass in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial testing whether creatine supplementation combined with twice-weekly resistance training can help maintain muscle mass and potentially slow cancer progression. The 52-week program aims to reduce fatigue, improve physical function, and enhance quality of life. This lifestyle intervention is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Enzalutamide With or Without Radium-223 in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial comparing enzalutamide alone versus enzalutamide combined with Radium-223 (a radioactive treatment targeting bone metastases) in mCRPC patients. The study is no longer recruiting new patients but remains active. Radium-223 delivers targeted radiation to bone tumors while enzalutamide blocks testosterone's effects.

items.title: AMO959 With Lutetium-177 PSMA and Hormonal Therapy for mCRPC
items.summary: A Phase 1b/2 trial testing AMO959 combined with lutetium-177 PSMA therapy (Pluvicto) and hormonal therapy in mCRPC patients who failed one prior hormonal agent. The study will evaluate safety and effectiveness of this combination approach. Currently recruiting patients who may or may not have received prior chemotherapy.

items.title: Tulmimetostat With Darolutamide or Abiraterone in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial evaluating tulmimetostat combined with either darolutamide or abiraterone in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (cancer that still responds to hormone therapy). This is an earlier disease stage than castration-resistant, aiming to prevent progression. Study is recruiting.

items.title: Multi-Target Radioligand Therapy for Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1 trial using imaging to identify which protein target (PSMA, SSTR2, or GRPR) is most expressed on tumor cells, then delivering matched radioligand therapy for up to 6 cycles in patients with metastatic neuroendocrine prostate cancer. This aggressive cancer variant often doesn't respond to standard treatments. Study is no longer recruiting.

items.title: Adding Docetaxel to Hormonal Therapy and Apalutamide for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing standard treatment (hormonal therapy plus apalutamide) against the same treatment with added docetaxel chemotherapy in metastatic prostate cancer patients. The ASPIRE trial aims to determine if adding chemotherapy early improves outcomes. This is a large, important trial currently recruiting.

items.title: SX-682 Plus Enzalutamide in Resistant Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial testing SX-682 combined with enzalutamide in mCRPC patients whose cancer progressed despite prior hormonal therapy. The study is recruiting men whose cancer has become resistant to androgen receptor pathway inhibitors, seeking to overcome this resistance through a novel mechanism.

items.title: First Taiwan Study of Terbium-161 PSMA Radioligand Therapy
items.summary: A Phase 1 dose-escalation trial evaluating 161Tb-PSMA-I&T, a next-generation radioligand therapy using Terbium-161 instead of Lutetium-177, in Taiwanese men with mCRPC. Terbium-161 may offer enhanced tumor-killing effects. The study will assess safety, dosing, and preliminary effectiveness while recruiting patients.

items.title: Genetic Testing to Guide Treatment in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial using genetic testing of tumor samples to assign patients to targeted treatments including valemetostat (EZH1/EZH2 inhibitor), carboplatin, or cabazitaxel based on specific DNA/RNA mutations. The PREDICT trial aims to match patients with the most effective therapy for their cancer's genetic profile. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Abiraterone as First-Line Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing olaparib (PARP inhibitor) plus abiraterone versus placebo plus abiraterone as first-line treatment for mCRPC patients who haven't received chemotherapy or new hormonal agents at the mCRPC stage. This large trial is no longer recruiting but remains active, evaluating whether adding a DNA-repair inhibitor improves outcomes.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide With Abiraterone in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial comparing two doses of luxdegalutamide (JSB462) combined with abiraterone versus standard hormonal therapy in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and will help select the best dose for a potential Phase 3 trial in earlier-stage disease.

items.title: PSCA-CAR T Cell Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1 trial testing genetically engineered immune cells (CAR T cells) that target PSCA protein on prostate cancer cells in mCRPC patients. The study is no longer recruiting and aims to determine the safest dose and evaluate how well these modified T cells can recognize and kill cancer cells.

items.title: Abiraterone, Olaparib, or Both in DNA Repair-Deficient Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial comparing abiraterone alone, olaparib alone, or both drugs combined in mCRPC patients whose tumors have mutations in DNA repair genes (ATM, BRCA1/2, and others). The study is no longer recruiting and tests whether targeting DNA repair defects improves treatment outcomes in genetically selected patients.

items.title: A-CAR032 CAR T Cell Therapy in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1 first-in-human trial of A-CAR032, an investigational CAR T cell therapy, in mCRPC patients who progressed after hormonal therapy and are ineligible for standard treatment. The study is recruiting and will evaluate safety, effectiveness, and feasibility of this novel immunotherapy approach.

items.title: Lutetium-177 PSMA With Liver-Directed Therapy for Liver Metastases
items.summary: A Phase 1b trial combining lutetium-177 PSMA therapy with liver-directed treatments in mCRPC patients with liver metastases who progressed on hormonal therapy. The study is recruiting and aims to determine if targeting liver metastases specifically while giving systemic radioligand therapy is safe and effective.

items.title: AZD5305 With Hormonal Agents in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial evaluating AZD5305 (a PARP inhibitor) combined with new hormonal agents in metastatic prostate cancer patients. The study is no longer recruiting and assesses safety, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary effectiveness of this DNA repair-targeting combination approach.

items.title: Success and Limitations of PSMA Radioligand Therapy: Expert Perspective
items.summary: A nuclear medicine review discussing lutetium-177 PSMA therapy's achievements and challenges in advanced prostate cancer. The article highlights rapid pain relief and high response rates as successes, but notes that nearly all patients eventually progress despite initial favorable responses. Emphasizes the need for interdisciplinary research to improve outcomes through molecular imaging and adaptive treatment strategies.

items.title: USP2 Protein Drives Therapy Resistance in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Research identifying USP2 as a protein that increases when prostate cancer becomes resistant to hormonal therapies. USP2 stabilizes cancer-promoting proteins and helps cancer cells survive both hormonal treatments and chemotherapy. The study found USP2 is elevated in aggressive, castration-resistant tumors and associated with neuroendocrine features and docetaxel resistance.

items.title: Bavdegalutamide Plus Abiraterone Phase 1b Trial Results
items.source: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
items.summary: A Phase 1b trial tested bavdegalutamide (ARV-110), an oral drug that degrades androgen receptors, combined with abiraterone in metastatic prostate cancer patients experiencing PSA progression on abiraterone. The combination showed acceptable safety with some patients achieving PSA control and remaining on treatment for extended periods. This novel approach targets resistant disease.

items.title: 2025 Advances in Radiopharmaceutical Therapy for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A comprehensive review of major developments in radiopharmaceutical therapy for prostate cancer during 2025. The field has evolved from pain management with radium-223 to cancer-directed treatments with PSMA-targeted therapies. The article discusses the rapid expansion following approval of prostate-specific membrane antigen targeted imaging and therapy options.

items.title: Terbium-161 PSMA Therapy After Lutetium-177 PSMA Treatment Progression
items.summary: A study of 15 mCRPC patients who received terbium-161 PSMA therapy after their cancer progressed on lutetium-177 PSMA treatment. Terbium-161 emits additional low-energy electrons that may enhance effectiveness. This exploratory evaluation provides early clinical insights on using an alternative radioligand after progression on standard PSMA therapy.

items.title: Combined Radium-223 and Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy Case Report
items.summary: A case report of an advanced mCRPC patient treated with combined radium-223 (alpha radiation for bone metastases) and lutetium-177 PSMA therapy (beta radiation). The combination was well tolerated with mild side effects initially showing favorable response, though later progression occurred. Demonstrates feasibility and safety of dual alpha/beta radioligand therapy in heavily treated patients.

items.title: Radium-223 After Lutetium-177 PSMA: Safety and Efficacy Study
items.summary: A multi-institutional study of 21 mCRPC patients who received Radium-223 after lutetium-177 PSMA therapy. Only 19% completed all 6 planned cycles, with most stopping due to disease progression. The study found significant blood toxicity including anemia and low platelet counts in many patients, raising concerns about sequencing these radioligand therapies.

items.title: Real-World Canadian Experience With Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy
items.source: Canadian Urological Association journal = Journal de l'Association des urologues du Canada
items.summary: A study of the first 50 mCRPC patients treated with lutetium-177 PSMA therapy in a Canadian center, reporting on treatment timelines, effectiveness, and safety. The real-world data provides insights into how this therapy performs outside of clinical trials, including wait times from referral to treatment and actual patient outcomes in routine practice.
